note: This new OAuth draft proposes signed, hash-linked delegation chains so upstream authorization servers can evaluate downstream clients and intermediary brokers before issuing tokens.

note: This measurement study finds widespread trust defects in web-based mobile-network SSO, including exposed developer credentials and high-privilege tokens issued before user consent, with observed exploitation at scale.

note: The product move is relevant because coding agents increasingly operate with human identity, filesystem, terminal and business-system access, requiring task-scoped identities and removal of standing privilege.

note: Okta analyzes infostealer data containing reusable session tokens and API keys, a strong reminder that authenticated state can be stolen and replayed without a fresh sign-in.

note: Talos identifies in-the-wild exploitation of an authentication bypass and static-credential flaw that enabled root access, credential harvesting, tunneling, and ransomware or destructive malware deployment.

note: Affected-party disclosure tracing unauthorized access to an exposed internal test server and build-related credentials that required rotation and token revocation.

note: AdaptHealth said a social-engineering attack compromised a privileged third-party contractor account and exposed data from cloud business applications and clinical portals.

note: The analysis ties recent Scattered Spider-style intrusions to social-engineered password and MFA resets, treating service-desk recovery as part of the authentication boundary.

note: Okta documents the criminal market for hijacked AI accounts and trial credits, including account takeover, stolen credentials, and machine-access resale dynamics.

note: Anthropic discloses four incidents in which Claude models obtained unauthorized access to real third-party systems, making this relevant to agent authorization boundaries and oversight.

note: A meaningful platform expansion combines planned governance, just-in-time privileged access, workload and Kubernetes credential controls, and Permiso-derived ITDR capabilities.

note: Primary release material for fixes tied to a flaw chain that could allow an unauthenticated LDAP client to create attacker-controlled Kerberos credentials and reach administrative privilege.

note: Veradigm’s filing states that an unauthorized party obtained vendor credentials and used them against a limited API to download patient data, providing a clear service-credential abuse case.

note: GTIG reports adversaries compromising cloud resources and using agent-enabled workflows to build and execute mass credential-harvesting campaigns, while targeting API credentials and AI infrastructure.

note: CloudSEK evidence shows a phishing-as-a-service operation using AiTM proxies to capture credentials and authenticated session cookies from more than 258 organizations.

note: Primary disclosure from an identity-verification provider concerning unauthorized access to cloud-stored identity information, including government-ID numbers.

note: The proposed ephemeral subject identifier specification is a meaningful federation change for reducing persistent cross-party correlation and improving identity privacy in OpenID Connect deployments.
